title: From Behind the Camera to Centre Frame: Lokesh Kanagaraj's 'DC' Trailer Drops at Cannes and Tamil Cinema Loses Its Mind
excerpt: The architect of the Lokesh Cinematic Universe makes his acting debut in a blood-soaked Devdas reimagining — and the trailer, premiered at Cannes on May 15, has the internet asking one question: can the director who made Vijay and Kamal act actually act himself?
body:
The man who built modern Tamil cinema's most ambitious shared universe has done something no one saw coming. Lokesh Kanagaraj — the director behind *Kaithi*, *Vikram*, and the sprawling Lokesh Cinematic Universe (LCU) that turned Kamal Haasan, Vijay, and Suriya into interconnected franchise pieces — has stepped in front of the camera.

And he didn't do it quietly. The trailer for *DC*, his acting debut, premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on May 15, 2026.

## The Pitch: Devdas Meets Goodfellas

*DC* is directed by Arun Matheswaran, the man behind *Rocky* and *Captain Miller*, a filmmaker whose visual signature is drenched in blood, dust, and moral ambiguity. In Matheswaran's hands, the classic Devdas story — the doomed lover who drowns himself in vice — becomes a full-throated gangster epic.

Lokesh plays a character described as a "modern Devdas," but this isn't Sanjay Leela Bhansali's gilded tragedy. The trailer opens with Lokesh, bearded and dead-eyed, walking through a rain-soaked Madurai street, and closes with him unloading a revolver into a dinner table. Wamiqa Gabbi co-stars as the woman caught in his orbit — equal parts anchor and accelerant. The chemistry in the trailer's fleeting glimpses is taut, charged, and deliberately withholding.

Anirudh Ravichander's score, pulsating underneath every frame, does what Anirudh scores do: it makes you feel like you're watching something monumental even when a man is just lighting a cigarette.

## Why Cannes Matters

The decision to premiere the trailer at Cannes rather than at a Mumbai multiplex event or a Hyderabad fan gathering was deliberate and strategic. Tamil cinema has been building its global footprint for years — *Jai Bhim* went to the Oscars shortlist, *Ponniyin Selvan* was a box-office phenomenon across diaspora markets, and *Vikram* turned "Once upon a time there was a ghost" into a line that NRI kids quote at dinner tables in New Jersey.

But premiering a commercial trailer at Cannes signals something bigger. It says: this isn't festival cinema looking for approval. This is mainstream Indian cinema demanding the world's biggest stage — and getting it.

Pa Ranjith, who was at Cannes for a separate project, publicly praised the trailer. "The visuals are extraordinary," he wrote on social media, adding that Wamiqa Gabbi "has something special in every frame."

## Can Lokesh Kanagaraj Actually Act?

The question hanging over *DC* isn't whether the film will be well-made — Arun Matheswaran's track record speaks for itself. It's whether Lokesh, who has spent his career coaxing career-best performances out of others, can deliver one himself.

Early reactions to the trailer suggest he can. Film Twitter — admittedly the most excitable court of opinion on the planet — has been unanimous: the restraint in his eyes, the physical stillness that erupts into sudden violence, the way he holds a frame without fidgeting. These are not the hallmarks of a director doing a vanity cameo. This looks like someone who has studied acting the way he studies screenplay structure — obsessively, from first principles.

The film is expected to release theatrically in late 2026, with a simultaneous five-language launch in Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada, and Malayalam. OTT rights are rumoured to be with Amazon Prime Video, which would make it instantly accessible to the enormous South Indian diaspora audiences in the US, UK, Canada, and the Middle East who have made Tamil cinema their weekend ritual.

## For NRI Fans: Mark Your Calendar

If you're part of the diaspora that turned *Vikram* into a $5 million overseas earner and made Lokesh Kanagaraj a household name in Scarborough and Fremont alike, *DC* is the film you'll be booking FDFS tickets for. The trailer alone has clocked 18 million YouTube views in 48 hours.

The theatrical release date hasn't been confirmed, but distributors in North America and the UK are already positioning it as a major event release. Don't be surprised if your local AMC or Cineplex has a Tamil-language screening on day one.

This is Lokesh Kanagaraj's biggest gamble. And if the trailer is anything to go by, the man who made everyone else look like a star might just be one himself.
